summary.overview: Bookshop is a React web app calling a FastAPI service. The API searches a catalogue index run by another team, and places orders by charging the card at an external payment provider and then inserting the order into its own PostgreSQL database. Docker compose deploys the web app, API and database; the search index and payment provider are outside this repo.
findings: The card is charged before the order is saved (api/bookshop/orders/service.py:31-32); a failed insert leaves a paid order that was never recorded.
PAYMENTS_URL is set in docker-compose.yml:12 but the code ignores it: the charges URL is hardcoded (api/bookshop/payments/client.py:3), so the setting does nothing.
The web app sends a hardcoded placeholder card token (web/src/main.tsx:15), so checkout is not real payment collection yet.
Services are built at import time (api/bookshop/main.py:7-8) and read DATABASE_URL and SEARCH_URL then, so the API cannot start without them.
POST /api/orders accepts an untyped dict and indexes keys directly (api/bookshop/main.py:17-18); missing fields raise a 500 rather than a validation error.
Neither the payment call nor the search call sets a timeout or handles failure (api/bookshop/payments/client.py:10, api/bookshop/search/index.py:13).
recommendations: Save the order as pending before charging, then mark it paid, so a failed insert is recoverable.
Read the payments URL from PAYMENTS_URL, or remove the unused setting.
Use a pydantic model for the order request and set timeouts on outbound calls.
